headline: Models infer unmeasured protein, chromatin and isoform layers from measured omics
label: Cross Modal Molecular Layer Inference
summary: TSNR and MorphoProt predict spatial protein from RNA, while MUTUAL, IsoPrism and Top2All reconstruct chromatin, isoform and full-transcriptome layers.
synthesis: The dominant thread is predicting an unmeasured molecular layer from a co-measured one. For spatial proteomics, TSNR regresses protein abundance from spatial transcriptomics using protein-specific center signals plus compact broad molecular context under a Huber loss. MorphoProt instead conditions on RNA via cross-attention over multiscale histology and tissue neighborhoods, outperforming RNA-only baselines. HistoTx early-fuses H&E patches with transcript tokens at arbitrary resolution through continued self-supervised training. Beyond spatial data, MUTUAL aligns frozen single-cell foundation model embeddings into a shared RNA–ATAC latent space trained on 3.0M multiome cells. IsoPrism allocates isoform proportions from short-read single-cell and spatial transcriptomes, and Top2All benchmarks Geneformer-based reconstruction of whole transcriptomes from sparse high-expression genes. A secondary oncology strand covers survival and stratification: CMVAE, GOTSurv (unbalanced optimal transport), DMG-PoE (product-of-experts under missing modalities), HHRM hierarchical subtyping, and MODAE+ cell-line-to-tumour drug-response transfer. The newer emphasis is RNA-conditioned inference of protein rather than image-only prediction.
